newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian CBR 1996 profits seen higher.
newsitem.headline: Belgian CBR 1996 profits seen higher.

text.p: Leading Belgian cement maker CBR, a unit of Germany's Heidelberger Zement, will unveil higher profits on Thursday for 1996 than in the previous year, analysts said on Monday.
The company made a consolidated net profit of 5.02 billion francs in 1995.

"We expect a new increase in earnings for 1996," Generale Bank analyst Luc Van Der Elst said. "For 1996 we put earnings per share at 200 francs, that is up 8.7 percent on 1995. For 1997 we have it at between 220 and 225 francs."
Van Der Elst's EPS estimates were in line with consensus forecasts on Reuters Securities 3000.

Analysts agreed the sudden surge in cement prices in California, depressed for years, and income from CBR's Polish investments would be the main factors helping the firm buck the depressed state of the western European construction industry.
"But, as in the first half, financial items and taxation will also help the CBR figures," BBL analyst Jean-Marie Cauchetaux said.
He put earnings per share at 214 francs in 1996 and 233 in 1997 -- slightly above the market.
CBR bought 60 percent of Polish aggregates company Zielonogorskie Kopalnie Surowcow Mineralnych (ZKSM) in September through its Gorazdze SA unit.
In 1995 ZKSM sold 2.7 million tonnes of aggregates for 33.3 million zlotys, or around 315 million Belgian francs.
Analysts did not expect any impact on CBR's 1996 results from its investments during the year in Poland and China, but said these would feed through to results in 1997.
Early last year CBR took a 97.7 percent stake in Turkey's Canakkale Cimento Sanayii AS -- immediately adding 20 percent to the total cement capacity of the group.

Half of the stake was swapped a few months later for a 30 percent stake in Turkey's Akcimento. As of October 1, the merged entity was renamed Akcansa, 79.4 percent owned in equal parts by the CBR and Sabanci groups.
Akcansa has annual cement production capacity of 5.4 million tonnes, of which 30 percent is exported.

Analysts expected CBR shares to get a new lease of life from the results. With a year-to-date rise of just under 17 percent, they have mildly outperformed the Brussels Bel-20's percent rise and the construction sector's near 14 percent rise.
"The share has been relatively stable recently, but it could be in for another good performance now," Generale Bank's Van Der Elst said.
"Compared with other European construction shares it is cheap and it has good earnings prospects," he added.
At 1315 GMT the CBR share was up 15 francs at 3,385. It hit a year high of 3,500 francs on January 21.
